## The puzzle

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

The transatlantic press contradicts itself by dimension. Macron invoked Article 42.7 on European soil. Spain refused Rota/Morón for offensive Iran operations. Germany announced a 460,000-troop target. But EU LNG dependence is now ~60% US-sourced, the EU said nothing about China's 2 May blocking statute, and EU sanctions architecture stays aligned with the US. Decoupling on diplomacy and security; deepening on finance. Which is the *real* trajectory?

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

The transatlantic press has contradicted itself by dimension since 28 February 2026. *On diplomacy*: EU foreign-policy chief Kallas said the US war "shaken the transatlantic relationship to its foundation." Macron invoked Article 42.7 (the EU Treaty's mutual defense clause) in Athens on 26 April. Spain refused Rota/Morón for offensive Iran operations; Poland refused Patriot redeployment; the E3 (UK/France/Germany) issued a joint statement on 1 March that did not endorse the US strikes. *On security*: Macron announced an 8-country aircraft deployment framework; Germany's mid-2030s target is 460,000 troops; the Enders €50bn/year German expert plan names 10 capability gaps to close. *On finance*: US LNG dependence has now deepened to ~60% of EU LNG imports; EU silent on China's 2 May 2026 blocking statute; EU IRGC designation 29 January demonstrated EU-US sanctions convergence rather than divergence; the renminbi alternative architecture remains too thin (~2% of FX reserves) to give EU firms a viable hedge. Which trajectory is real? A single-framework answer would say "decoupling" or "deepening" or "no real change." The empirical record matches *none* of the unitary answers cleanly. The puzzle Q9 sets: what's actually happening, and which framework captures it?

The diplomatic / institutional dimension fits [Pape's soft-balancing]{.gloss data-gloss="pape-soft-balancing"} cleanly: Article 42.7 invocation, Spain's Rota/Morón refusal, EU IRGC designation friction, "quiet quitting" of US Iran policy through institutional channels rather than military counterbalancing. The security architecture dimension is [Posen F3-trending-from-F2]{.gloss data-gloss="posen-restraint"}: Macron 8-country aircraft framework + Germany 460,000-troop target + Enders €50bn/year plan are *announced* (level 1-2 in a five-level pipeline) but not yet *executed* (level 3-4); the dimension is in transition with milestone test at end-Q4 2027. ## Methodology — META rule 7 (NEW) and the principled-vs-rescue distinction

This chapter applies the project's 8-step protocol. The devil's-advocate pass forced the most consequential methodological move in the project so far: the original synthesis *rejected* dimension-specificity as a procedural compliance with the no-rescue META rules (developed in Q5/Q12.5/Q11 to prevent unitary-framework rescue). The DA showed the rejection was itself a procedural error — Q9's framework-domain mappings (Pape's institutional/diplomatic, Posen's security architecture, Farrell-Newman's interdependence) are *literature-derived* and pre-analysis, not invented post-hoc. The principled-vs-rescue distinction became META rule 7: dimension-specificity is the substantive finding when framework-domain mappings are *pre-analysis*; dimension-specificity is rescue when sub-structure is invented *after* the analysis to save a unitary framework. The rule is BIDIRECTIONAL — it applies forward (Q9, Q7, Q10) and was generated by reflection on prior failures (Q5, Q12.5, Q11). The mechanism inventory collapsed from five to three to two (σ + ε); the synthesis's three mechanisms reduced via DA Critique 9 to two.
:::

[**Three dimensions, three different stories.** *Diplomatic* — Article 42.7, Spain base refusal, EU IRGC designation. *Security* — Macron framework, German 460k target, Enders €50bn plan. *Financial* — US LNG ~60% of EU imports, EU silent on China Blocking Rules, sanctions alignment. The dimensions move in different directions; the unitary-framework answers do not fit.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Three dimensions, three different stories.** The standard transatlantic-relationship literature presents single-framework answers: *Ikenberry-with-erosion* says the architecture persists (institutions are sticky); *Pape soft-balancing* says secondary states quietly delay-and-frustrate; *Posen forced-autonomy* says Europe builds operational alternatives under hegemonic unreliability. The 2026 case is awkward for each: institutional persistence is correct in finance but contradicted by Spain's basing refusal and Article 42.7 invocation; soft-balancing fits the diplomatic record but understates the costed German rearmament plans; forced-autonomy describes the security trajectory but cannot accommodate Europe's deepening dollar/SWIFT/LNG dependence. The empirical record points at *different frameworks for different dimensions* — which the standard methodological discipline (avoid Lakatos rescue) would normally pre-reject as ad-hoc sub-structure. The Q9 finding's contribution is to show this pre-rejection is itself wrong when the framework-domain mappings are *literature-derived*. Pape's 2005 *Soft Balancing against the United States* is natively about institutional-instrument behavior; Posen's *Restraint* (2014) is natively about security-architecture choices; Farrell-Newman's *Weaponized Interdependence* (2019) is natively about financial-architecture chokepoints. The frameworks have non-overlapping natural domains in the literature *before* the analysis. The dimension-specific finding is therefore principled, not rescue.
:::
:::

Institutional, dispersed, deliberately ambiguous — what Pape predicts secondary states do when the unipolar leader pursues aggressive unilateral policies.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Diplomatic / institutional dimension → [Pape soft-balancing]{.gloss data-gloss="pape-soft-balancing"} (2005) cleanly applied.** The observed European behavior fits Pape's predictions point-by-point. *Entangling diplomacy*: EU foreign-policy chief Kallas's "shaken the transatlantic relationship to its foundation" framing; Macron's Article 42.7 invocation in Athens on 26 April 2026 (the EU treaty's mutual-defense clause, never previously invoked over a US action); the E3 joint statement of 1 March that did not endorse the US strikes; EU IRGC designation 29 January demonstrated alignment on sanctions but also institutional friction over conduct; Spain's legal-sovereignty framing of base refusal. *Territorial denial*: Spain's Rota and Morón closure for offensive Iran operations *specifically* (rather than general basing); Polish Patriot redeployment refusal; selective German and Italian basing constraints throughout the war. *Style of engagement*: institutional, dispersed, deliberately ambiguous — what Politico's Momtaz captured as "quiet quitting" of US Iran policy. Not military counterbalancing; not full institutional rupture; selective non-cooperation through legal and procedural channels. *These behaviors do not require capability-substitution and do not require US-as-threat classification.* They are exactly what Pape (2005) predicts secondary states do when the unipolar leader pursues aggressive unilateral policies: institutional friction without military rupture.
:::

::: {.deep-only}
**Security architecture dimension → [Posen F3-trending-from-F2]{.gloss data-gloss="posen-restraint"} in transition.** The dimension is genuinely contested between the F2 reading (current equilibrium of institutional persistence with erosion) and the F3 reading (trending toward forced-autonomy). *F2 evidence (current equilibrium)*: 14% troop reduction announced but not yet executed; Tomahawk redeployment plan canceled but reversible; 86% of US forces remain in Germany; NATO Article 5 reaffirmed by Rutte to Türkiye; institutional NATO architecture intact; allied basing for non-Iran missions presumably still available. *F3 evidence (trending state)*: Macron's 8-country aircraft deployment framework (Île Longue speech, 2 March); Germany's 460,000-troop target by mid-2030s (Brookings/Stelzenmüller); the Enders €50bn/year German expert plan with 10 named capability gaps; expected NATO 5%-of-GDP-by-2035 target; the Carnegie/Daalder/Stelzenmüller/Lute analyst convergence on autonomy-as-required. *The dimension is genuinely contested.* F3 is the most likely trajectory if costed plans execute (level 1-2 → level 3-4 transition), but execution risk is non-trivial: the historical base rate of European-defense-autonomy-named-in-expert-paper to budgeted-and-executed-program is below 50%. The 1999 Helsinki rapid-reaction force, the 2003 European Security Strategy, and Macron's 2017 Sorbonne speeches are precedents that did not execute. *Treat the dimension as F2-currently / F3-trending, with a milestone test at end-Q4 2027 (€50bn benchmark, level-3 budget appropriation in at least one of France/Germany/Poland).*
:::

Europe is *more* US-dependent in finance/energy in May 2026 than it was in February — even as it visibly decouples on security and diplomacy.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Financial / interdependence dimension → [Ikenberry-with-erosion]{.gloss data-gloss="ikenberry-institutional-persistence"} bounded by [Farrell-Newman γ]{.gloss data-gloss="farrell-newman-interdependence"} structural trap.** The empirical record points in the opposite direction from the diplomatic and security dimensions. *US LNG dependence deepening*: now ~60% of EU LNG imports (per Demarais / ECFR, computed from Eurostat); LNG ~50% of EU gas; €24-25bn EU fossil-fuel import overspend over winter 2025-26 (Bruegel + Carbon Brief + Commission convergent). *EU silent on China Blocking Rules*: as of 10 May 2026, eight days after Beijing's 2 May blocking statute over Hengli plus four other teapot refineries, there has been no EU institutional statement. This is the largest single corpus gap and confirms that Europe is structurally trapped in dollar/SWIFT/secondary-sanctions architecture — it has no operational alternative to align with. *Renminbi alternative architecture too thin*: 80% of global oil still dollar-settled; renminbi only ~2% of FX reserves. EU firms have no viable hedge against US sanctions architecture. *EU sanctions architecture aligned with US*: EU IRGC designation 29 January 2026 demonstrated EU/US sanctions convergence rather than divergence — the institutional friction is over Iran policy *conduct*, not over the underlying architecture. *Bruegel METSAF analysis* (7 May 2026): EU institutional response to energy shock is fragmenting (France + Germany together over 50% of CISAF; Hungary nearly 2% of GDP) rather than consolidating. This is the dimension where Farrell-Newman γ is most clearly load-bearing. Europe cannot operationally decouple from US economic architecture in any reasonable timeframe; the structural trap holds. Ikenberry's "institutions persist with erosion" describes the architecture's status well; the *erosion* part is real (selective rules contested) but the *persistence* part is structurally enforced (no alternative exists at operational scale).
:::
:::

[The five-level pipeline distinguishes *announced* from *executed* European defense commitments. Most 2026 commitments sit at L1-L2 (named in expert papers; endorsed by ministers). F3 forced-autonomy requires L3-L4 (approved in coalition treaty; appropriated in budget). The milestone test at end-Q4 2027 asks: is at least one of {France, Germany, Poland} at L4 (budget appropriation) for Enders-paper-named capability gaps?]{.concise-only}
[**The five-level commitment-execution pipeline.** A critical methodological move (per DA Critique 7): distinguish what is *announced* from what is *executed*. Most current European defense commitments sit at L1-L2 — named in expert papers (Enders €50bn/year, Macron 8-country aircraft framework) or endorsed by ministers (Germany 460,000-troop target). F3 forced-autonomy requires at minimum L3-L4 (approved in coalition treaty; appropriated in budget). The historical base rate of L1-L2 commitments reaching L4-L5 execution is below 50% — Helsinki 1999 rapid-reaction force, European Security Strategy 2003, Macron's 2017 Sorbonne speeches are all precedents that did not execute. The pre-registered milestone test at end-Q4 2027: is at least one of {France, Germany, Poland} at Level 3 (budget appropriation) for Enders-paper-named capability gaps? If yes for ≥ 2 member states, F3 security dimension validates and the dimension moves from F3-trending to F3-current. If no, F3 was over-projected and reduce P(security dimension F3-trending) by 0.15.]{.deep-only}

## Pre-mortem {#pre-mortem}

The most likely ways the analysis will be wrong:

1. **The dimension-specific finding becomes F3 uniform by 2027-28** (P ≈ 0.20-0.25). Costed European security plans execute and the F3-trending security dimension crystallizes. Pre-mortem signal: by end-Q4 2027, ≥ 2 member states at level-3 budget appropriation for Enders-paper capability gaps.

2. **The dimension-specific finding becomes F2-with-erosion uniform by 2027-28** (P ≈ 0.30-0.35). Costed security plans do not execute, Press revisionism plays out empirically through Russian non-probing of Eastern flank, and Trump-successor partially reverses operational decoupling.

3. **A novel framework emerges (Configuration F-style)** (P ≈ 0.10). Possibly tied to EU-China bilateral arrangement on Iran-related sanctions, or a French-led European nuclear architecture more operationally substantive than current evidence suggests.

4. **Mechanism σ is wrong**: the structural-constraint mechanism could turn out to be reversible if European publics become more anti-Iran (e.g., further European casualties from Iran-aligned proxies after the Frion in Erbil), enabling elite re-alignment with US (P ≈ 0.10).

5. **The Iran war ends near-term**, removing wartime stress and revealing that the European decoupling moves were tactical (Iran-specific) rather than structural (P ≈ 0.10-0.15).

6. **Unforeseen Russia move (escalation against Eastern flank)** restores NATO Article 5 cohesion in observable ways and reveals that the F3-trending security dimension was a paper finding (P ≈ 0.05).

**Lowest-confidence claim**: that European behavior is genuinely *dimensionally* structured rather than reflecting a single underlying mechanism (σ structural-constraint-bounded autonomy reorientation) that produces apparently-different surface behaviors in different dimensions. If pressed: P(genuine dimension-specificity) ≈ 0.55; P(σ-single-mechanism producing dimensional surface) ≈ 0.30. These are not the same thing methodologically.

## Pre-1979 historical lineage

The 2026 transatlantic decoupling pattern is the full inversion of a 73-year-old structural template. In 1953, the **UK was the senior strategic partner** in the operation against Mosaddegh — MI6 originated Operation Boot; the CIA's Operation Ajax executed it. The Anglo-American team (Roosevelt-Wilber-Schwarzkopf + Zaehner-Derbyshire-Rashidian) was a *European-led* operation in which the US played the operational-follower role with greater resources. The 2026 Israel-led, US-followed coalition (Q11) is a structural homology, but the European role has *collapsed entirely* from senior strategic partner to marginal third party — Macron's Article 42.7 invocation in Athens is institutional friction, not strategic leadership.

This deepens Q9's [Pape soft-balancing]{.gloss data-gloss="pape-soft-balancing"} reading for the diplomatic dimension. **European powers' treatment of Iran has a 113-year pattern of marginality** — WWI is the canonical earlier instance. Iran fielded no soldiers in WWI, lost ~1 million dead (from famine and Spanish flu, out of ~9 million population), and *was not allowed to bring grievances to the Paris Peace Conference*. The 1907 Anglo-Russian Convention had already partitioned Iran into spheres of influence without Iranian consent. The 2026 European posture of soft-balancing through institutional friction — without independent operational capacity — is consistent with this multi-decade pattern of European Iran-policy as derivative or absent. The F3-trending security dimension Q9 reads at P=0.15 needs to overcome a long historical pattern of European-strategic-autonomy projects (1999 Helsinki, 2003 ESS, 2017 Macron Sorbonne) that did not execute.

**Full pre-1979 context**: [Historical roots](../historical-roots.qmd).
